memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And God spoke to Israel in a vision at night and said, 'Jacob! Jacob!' 'Here I am,' he replied." — Gen 46:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls him twice by name — "Jacob! Jacob!" — the way you would call someone you love, urgently and personally.

That doubled name appears at some of the most tender moments in Scripture. "Abraham! Abraham!" on the mountain (Gen 22:11). "Moses! Moses!" at the burning bush (Ex 3:4). "Samuel! Samuel!" in the night (1 Sam 3:10). "Martha, Martha" from the lips of Jesus (Lk 10:41). It is not the voice of a distant deity issuing orders. It is the voice of someone who knows you.

Notice also which name God uses. Not Israel, the honourable covenant name, but Jacob — the old name, the one that means grasper, the name from before everything changed. God is not shaming him. He is meeting the whole man, past and all, exactly as he is.

Jacob's answer is simply, "Here I am." Available. Listening. Nothing complicated.

God still speaks to His people, chiefly through His Word, and He does not address us as strangers. The Good Shepherd calls His own sheep by name (Jn 10:3). He knows the name you are proud of and the name you would rather forget, and He calls you anyway.

The right response has not changed either. Here I am.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When did you last simply say "Here I am" to God and wait?
2. Does it comfort or unsettle you that God knows the parts of your past you would rather leave behind?
3. What might be crowding out your ability to hear Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You know me completely and still call me by name. Here I am. Quiet my heart so that I can listen to You today. Amen.
